about: What OpenAI-compatible servers really do, and how both harnesses cope. Each quirk is detected, handled, and — where marked — learned, so the next request does not trip it again. The CLI keeps what it learned in ~/.local/state/lembas/learned.json; LLeMbas on the model row or in process memory.

quirks.symptom: 400 or 422 to a request carrying stream_options
quirks.handling: retry once without it, before anything was streamed

quirks.symptom: an error whose text names the effort and says unexpected or supported (conformance/effort.json)
quirks.handling: retry once without an effort, before anything was streamed; narrow the model's efforts to those the message advertises

quirks.symptom: a top-level reasoning_effort is silently dropped
quirks.handling: send it top-level and as chat_template_kwargs.reasoning_effort (effort_style both)

quirks.symptom: prompt_progress {total, cache, processed, time_ms} frames before the reply
quirks.handling: ask for it, show how far the prompt has been read; a 400 to the field is learned and it is not asked again

quirks.symptom: reasoning arrives as reasoning_content, reasoning, or inline <think>/<thinking>/<reasoning> tags (conformance/think.json)
quirks.handling: all three read as reasoning; reasoning is never sent back as context

quirks.symptom: an error object inside a 200 event stream, sometimes as an unterminated last line
quirks.handling: read as the error it is, not as an empty reply
fragments without an index continue the last call

quirks.symptom: a loading banner streamed before the reply while the model loads
a 'model unloaded' frame mid-reply, when another client loaded a different model
quirks.handling: treated as a server error: retried once

quirks.symptom: a usage block of all zeros
quirks.handling: ignored; the count is estimated (marked ~) instead

quirks.symptom: /models lists ids without a context length
quirks.handling: ask llama-server's /props (through llama-swap's /upstream/<model>), Ollama's /api/show, else unknown — never assume one
